doc.title: Will Shade and Dewey Corley Interview, 1960-05-25

title: Later jug band members: Robert Carter, Jab Jones, Charlie Polk
summary: Shade lists who replaced original members, including Jab Jones on jug, and Charlie Polk, whom he taught the jug; Jab's work with Sleepy John Estes is discussed.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What about who took Weldon's place? Robert Carter. What did he play?
Dittor.
And who'd you get on the jug?
I had Jab Jones on the jug.
Oh. And did he play anything else?
He played piano.
You say he worked with Sleepy John Estes for a while?

Well, him and them recorded some records a while back. Around about 26 or 27, they made the record called The Diving Duck and The Brickish Jail. Something else they made, but I can't remember what else they made, but I know they made about two or three records.
Where do you think Sleepy John is now?
Brown with Tennessee the last time I heard from him. He done went blind now.
Mm-hmm. When did Charlie Polk come in there?
Charlie Polk, he was the first one who was with me. No, he was the second one who was with me after Roundhouse died. Mm-hmm.
And what did he play?
He played the jug. I learned him how to play the jug.
Well, when did Jab Jones come in? After him or before?
He come in after him.
Mm-hmm.
After Charlie died, then Jab Jones come in.
Yeah. Well, what instrument did he play with Sleepy John? He played the pound and jug. Both, huh?
Yeah.
